Agent 15 (15A/15B): 01C FT-03 is internally inconsistent with the debt thresholds it invokes. Its pass criterion 'external debt/GDP stabilises below the DSA threshold' compares a total, face-value external-debt ratio with LIC-DSF thresholds, which are defined on the present value of external public and publicly guaranteed debt (plus a PV total-public-debt benchmark). A financing gap (I/Y minus S/Y) maps to the current account and to total external liabilities including FDI and private debt, not to PPG debt. 02C has raised this and proposed FT-03a/b/c; 01C still lists its 02C input as 'missing in r1' although research/findings/02/02C-r1.json exists. Required: adopt a split test, or justify the single test; state the publicly financed share of the gap as a labelled assumption; use PV ratios only where a DSA PV series or documented discounting exists (02C-A2).

Agent 15 (15A): the exchange-rate construction mixes fiscal-year bases. 03A plans the historical INR/USD depreciation distribution on the Indian fiscal year (April-March annual averages from the RBI Handbook), while 01C SG-04 requires quartiles of rolling INR/USD depreciation aligned to the Nepal FY (mid-July to mid-July). Indian-FY annual averages cannot be re-aggregated to Nepal FY; daily or monthly FBIL/RBI reference rates are needed (as 03A-A2 allows for monthly series). Second, FT-09 requires project() to reproduce USD0 in the base year, but the base-year NPR/USD is the observed NRB middle rate while projected NPR/USD is peg ratio x INR/USD. The peg-identity residual must be carried or the splice breaks the identity. The rate type (NRB middle rate) is consistent across 01C, 03A, 05B and 22E.
